questions.question: The smell of hot food reaches a distance because:

options.text: sound waves carry the food smell

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**particles are continuously moving**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary reason the smell of hot food reaches a distance is that the **particles of matter** are **continuously moving**. This is a fundamental property of matter described by the **Kinetic Molecular Theory**. ***Hence, the correct statement is that particles are continuously moving.***
 
• In the case of **hot food**, the **temperature** is high, which significantly increases the **kinetic energy** of the **aroma particles** (volatile organic compounds) released from the food.
 
• When the **kinetic energy** increases, the **velocity** of these particles also increases, allowing them to mix rapidly with **air particles** and move across large distances in a short amount of time.
 
• This process of **intermixing** of particles of two different types of matter on their own is known as **diffusion**. The rate of **diffusion** is much faster in **gases** compared to liquids or solids.
 
• Regarding other options: **Sound waves** are mechanical waves that carry energy through vibrations, not chemical aromas. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Light energy** does not carry physical matter like aroma particles; it is an electromagnetic wave. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• While **temperature** affects the state of food, it does not increase the **weight** of the food in a way that makes smell travel; in fact, evaporation might slightly decrease the mass. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Diffusion:** It is the movement of particles from a region of **higher concentration** to a region of **lower concentration**. In gases, diffusion is extremely rapid due to high **particle speed** and large **intermolecular spaces**.
 
• **Kinetic Energy and Temperature:** The **average kinetic energy** of particles is **directly proportional** to the **absolute temperature** (measured in **Kelvin**). This explains why the smell of **cold food** does not reach us as quickly as the smell of **hot sizzling food**.
 
• **Brownian Motion:** This is the **random, zig-zag motion** of microscopic particles in a fluid (liquid or gas) resulting from their collision with the fast-moving atoms or molecules in the gas or liquid. This was first observed by **Robert Brown** in **1827**.
 
• **States of Matter:** The rate of diffusion follows the order: **Gases > Liquids > Solids**. Because gas particles have the least **intermolecular force of attraction**, they move most freely.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Volatility:** Only **volatile substances** produce a smell. When food is heated, more molecules transition into the **vapour phase**, increasing the **concentration** of aroma particles in the air.
 
• **Practical Examples:**
 
 
• The smell of a **perfume** spreading in a room is due to the **diffusion** of perfume vapours in the air.
 
• The smell of an **incense stick** (agarbatti) when lit reaches us even in another room because the **heat** increases the movement of its particles.
 
• **Dissolving potassium permanganate** in water shows diffusion in liquids, where the purple color spreads throughout the **beaker**.
 
 
 
• **Atmospheric Factors:** The speed at which a smell travels can also be influenced by **wind currents** and **convection**, but the underlying molecular mechanism remains the **continuous motion** and **diffusion** of particles.

questions.question:
Which of the following is true for suspension?

a. Suspension is a heterogeneous mixture.

b. The particles of a suspension scatter a beam of light passing through it.

c. The particles of a suspension can be seen by the naked eye.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a, b and c**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **suspension** is defined as a **heterogeneous mixture** in which the **solute particles** do not dissolve but remain **suspended** throughout the bulk of the medium. Unlike a solution, the components can be clearly distinguished. ***Hence, statement a is correct.***
 
• The **particles of a suspension** are large enough to be **seen by the naked eye**. This is due to their size being typically **greater than 1000 nm** (or **1 micrometer**) in diameter, which makes them physically distinct from the solvent. ***Hence, statement c is correct.***
 
• Suspensions exhibit the **Tyndall effect**, which is the **scattering of a beam of light** as it passes through the mixture. Because the particles are large, they collide with light waves and deflect them, making the **path of light visible**. ***Hence, statement b is correct.***
 
• If a suspension is left **undisturbed**, the particles will eventually **settle down** at the bottom of the container due to the **force of gravity**. This indicates that a suspension is **unstable** in nature.
 
• When the particles settle down, the mixture **loses its ability to scatter light**. Therefore, the Tyndall effect is only observed while the particles are still **actively suspended** in the medium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Separation Methods**: Since the particles in a **suspension** are relatively large and do not dissolve, they can be separated from the mixture using the process of **filtration**. The **residue** remains on the **filter paper** while the liquid passes through.
 
• **Common Examples**: Familiar examples of suspensions include **muddy water**, **chalk powder in water**, **sand in water**, and **flour mixed in water**. In these cases, the solid phase is clearly visible and eventually precipitates.
 
• **Comparison with Solutions**: In contrast to suspensions, a **true solution** is a **homogeneous mixture** where particle sizes are **less than 1 nm**. These particles cannot be seen by the naked eye and do not scatter light.
 
• **Comparison with Colloids**: **Colloids** sit between solutions and suspensions. Their particle size ranges from **1 nm to 1000 nm**. While they appear homogeneous, they are actually **heterogeneous** and do scatter light, but their particles **do not settle** under gravity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Particle Size**: The distinguishing factor for a suspension is a particle size **exceeding 1000 nm**. This size threshold is what allows the particles to be filtered and seen without a microscope.
 
• **Optical Properties**: The **visibility of the light path** is a key diagnostic tool in chemistry to differentiate between a **true solution** and a **suspension or colloid**.
 
• **Stability**: A suspension is **chemically unstable** because the **solute-solvent** interaction is not strong enough to overcome **gravitational pull** over time, leading to **sedimentation**.
 
• **State of Matter**: Suspensions can exist in various forms, such as **solids in liquids** (mud in water) or **solids in gases** (dust particles in the air).

questions.question: Which of the following statements about meristematic tissues is INCORRECT?

options.text: Cells are small, thin-walled, and densely cytoplasmic with large nuclei.
Meristematic cells are dead at maturity.
Meristematic tissues consist of actively dividing cells.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meristematic cells are dead at maturity.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meristematic tissues** consist of a group of **actively dividing cells** that help in the **increase of length and girth** of the plant. These cells continue to divide throughout the **life cycle** of the plant. ***Hence, the statement 'Meristematic tissues consist of actively dividing cells' is correct.***
 
• The cells of these tissues are **very active**, have **dense cytoplasm**, **thin cellulose walls**, and **prominent nuclei**. The thin walls facilitate **rapid cell division**. ***Hence, the statement 'Cells are small, thin-walled, and densely cytoplasmic with large nuclei' is correct.***
 
• Unlike animals, plants have localized regions of growth. Meristematic tissues are present in these **growth regions**, allowing plants to **grow indefinitely** or exhibit **lifelong growth**. ***Hence, the statement 'Enable lifelong growth in plants' is correct.***
 
• Meristematic cells are **living cells** because they need to be **metabolically active** to undergo **mitosis**. Cells that are **dead at maturity**, such as **sclerenchyma** or **xylem vessels**, serve structural or transport functions and cannot divide. ***Hence, the statement 'Meristematic cells are dead at maturity' is incorrect.***
 
• The **vacuoles** are usually **absent** in meristematic cells because these cells do not need to **store food** or waste materials, as they are constantly dividing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification by Position:**

 
 
• **Apical Meristem:** Located at the **growing tips of stems and roots**. Its primary function is to increase the **length** of the plant, known as **primary growth**.
 
• **Intercalary Meristem:** Found at the **base of leaves** or **internodes** (e.g., in **grasses**). It helps in the **regeneration** of parts removed by **grazing herbivores**.
 
• **Lateral Meristem:** Occurs on the **sides of the stem and root**. It is responsible for increasing the **thickness or girth** of the plant, known as **secondary growth**. Examples include **vascular cambium** and **cork cambium**.
 
 
 
• **Differentiation:**
 
 
• When cells produced by meristematic tissue take up a **permanent shape, size, and function**, they lose the **ability to divide**. This process is called **differentiation**, leading to the formation of **permanent tissues**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Permanent Tissues:**
 
 
• **Simple Permanent Tissue:** Includes **Parenchyma** (storage), **Collenchyma** (flexibility), and **Sclerenchyma** (strength/rigidity).
 
• **Complex Permanent Tissue:** Includes **Xylem** (water transport) and **Phloem** (food transport).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The term **"Meristem"** was coined by **C. Nageli** in **1858**.
 
• **Meristematic cells** lack **intercellular spaces**; they are **compactly arranged** to ensure structural continuity during rapid division.
 
• The **metabolic rate** in meristematic cells is **extremely high** because of the energy demands of **DNA replication** and **cytokinesis**.
 
• In **woody plants**, the **lateral meristem** adds layers of **secondary xylem (wood)** and **secondary phloem** each year, creating **annual rings** used to determine the **age of the tree**.

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT an agent of cross pollination?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Light**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cross-pollination**, also known as **allogamy**, involves the transfer of **pollen grains** from the **anther** of a flower of one plant to the **stigma** of a flower of another plant of the same species.
 
• To facilitate this transfer over a distance, plants rely on various **pollinating agents**, which are broadly classified into **abiotic** (non-living) and **biotic** (living) agents.
 
• **Wind** is a common **abiotic agent** of cross-pollination. Plants that use wind for pollination, such as **grasses**, **corn**, and many **conifers**, produce large quantities of light, non-sticky pollen. *Hence, statement 4 is a correct agent.*
 
• **Water** is another **abiotic agent**, primarily used by aquatic plants like **Vallisneria** and **Hydrilla**. In these cases, pollen grains are often long and needle-like to float and reach the stigma. *Hence, statement 2 is a correct agent.*
 
• **Animals** serve as the primary **biotic agents**. This includes **insects** (bees, butterflies), **birds** (sunbirds, hummingbirds), and **mammals** (bats). These animals are attracted to the flower's **nectar**, **color**, or **scent**. *Hence, statement 3 is a correct agent.*
 
• **Light** is an essential environmental factor for **photosynthesis** and **photoperiodism** (the physiological reaction of organisms to the length of night or day). While light influences **flowering time**, it does not act as a physical carrier to transport pollen grains from one plant to another. *Hence, statement 1 is NOT an agent of cross-pollination.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Anemophily (Wind Pollination):**

 
 
• Flowers are generally small, **inconspicuous**, and lack **nectar** or **scent**.
 
• The **pollen grains** are **light**, **dry**, and **smooth-walled** so they can be easily carried by the wind.
 
• The **stigma** is often **feathery** or **branched** to catch the airborne pollen.
 
 
 
• **Hydrophily (Water Pollination):**
 
 
• This is relatively rare, occurring in only about **30 genera** of **monocotyledons**.
 
• Pollen grains are protected from wetting by a **mucilaginous covering**.
 
 
 
• **Zoophily (Animal Pollination):**
 
 
• **Entomophily** refers specifically to pollination by **insects**. These flowers are usually **brightly colored** and **fragrant**.
 
• **Ornithophily** is pollination by **birds**, while **Chiropterophily** is pollination by **bats**.
 
• Pollinators receive a "reward" in the form of **pollen** or **nectar**.
 
 
 
• **Self-Pollination vs. Cross-Pollination:**
 
 
• **Self-pollination** (Autogamy) occurs within the same flower or between flowers of the same plant.
 
• **Cross-pollination** increases **genetic diversity** and leads to the production of stronger, more adaptable offspring.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Light's Role:** It is important to distinguish that **Light** triggers the **biological clock** of a plant to start the **reproductive phase**, but the actual transport of genetic material (pollen) requires a physical medium like air, water, or a living creature.
 
• **Evolutionary Adaptation:** Many plants have evolved specific **morphological features** to favor cross-pollination over self-pollination, such as **Dichogamy** (different maturation times of anther and stigma) or **Self-incompatibility**.

questions.question: The direction of the magnetic field at the centre of a current-carrying circular loop can be determined by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right-hand rule (curling fingers along current)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Right-hand rule (curling fingers along current)** is specifically used to find the direction of the **magnetic field** at the **centre** of a **circular loop**. According to this rule, if we curl the fingers of our **right hand** in the direction of the **current** flowing through the circular wire, the **thumb** will point in the direction of the **magnetic field** at the **center**. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*
 
• When the **current** flows in an **anti-clockwise** direction, the **magnetic field** lines emerge **outward** from the center of the loop, representing a **North Pole**.
 
• When the **current** flows in a **clockwise** direction, the **magnetic field** lines point **inward** (into the plane), representing a **South Pole**.
 
• The **magnetic field** produced by a **circular loop** is strongest at its **centre** because the field contributions from every small segment of the loop add up vectorially in the same direction at that point.
 
• This rule is often considered a variation of **Maxwell’s Right-Hand Grip Rule**, adapted for curved geometries to simplify the visualization of **electromagnetic** effects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fleming’s Left-Hand Rule:**

 
 
• This rule is primarily used to determine the direction of the **magnetic force** (motion) acting on a **conductor**.
 
• It states that if the **forefinger** points in the direction of the **magnetic field** and the **middle finger** in the direction of the **current**, then the **thumb** represents the direction of the **force** or **motion**. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect for finding field direction.*
 
 
 
• **Right-Hand Palm Rule:**
 
 
• This is a simplified method to find the direction of **magnetic force**.
 
• The **fingers** point in the direction of the **magnetic field**, the **thumb** points in the direction of the **velocity** of a positive charge (or current), and the **palm** faces the direction of the **magnetic force**. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Maxwell’s Corkscrew Rule:**
 
 
• Also known as the **Right-Hand Screw Rule**, it states that if a right-handed **corkscrew** is rotated such that it advances in the direction of the **current**, the direction of rotation of the **handle** gives the direction of the **magnetic field**.
 
• This is typically used for **straight conductors** to visualize the **concentric** field lines.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Magnetic Field Strength:** The magnitude of the **magnetic field (B)** at the **centre** of a **circular loop** of **radius r** carrying **current I** is given by the formula **B = (μ₀I) / (2r)**, where **μ₀** is the **permeability of free space** (approximately **4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A**).
 
• **Number of Turns:** If the circular coil has **n turns**, the **magnetic field** produced is **n times** as large as that produced by a single turn, because the **current** in each turn has the same direction and the **fields** add up.
 
• **Right-Hand Thumb Rule (for Straight Wires):** Often confused with the loop rule, here the **thumb** points along the **current** in a straight wire, and the **curled fingers** show the **circular magnetic field** lines around it. *Hence, statement 4 (referring to a "Left-hand" version) is scientifically incorrect as the left hand is not used for this convention.*
 
• **Biot-Savart Law:** This is the fundamental **mathematical law** used to derive the **magnetic field** for any current configuration, including **circular loops** and **solenoids**.

questions.question: Which of the following elements shows +2 valency?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Beryllium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Beryllium (Be)** is a chemical element with the **atomic number 4**. Its electronic configuration is **1s² 2s²**. Because it has **two electrons** in its outermost shell (valence shell), it easily loses these two electrons to achieve a stable electronic configuration similar to **Helium**, resulting in a **valency of +2**. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• **Lithium (Li)** is the third element in the periodic table with an **atomic number of 3**. Its electronic configuration is **1s² 2s¹**. It has only **one electron** in its valence shell, which it loses to form a **Li⁺ ion**, giving it a **valency of +1**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Hydrogen (H)** has the **atomic number 1** and an electronic configuration of **1s¹**. It requires one electron to complete its duplet or can lose its single electron. Therefore, it typically exhibits a **valency of 1** (+1 or -1). ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Helium (He)** has an **atomic number of 2** and a configuration of **1s²**. Since its K-shell is already completely filled (attaining a **stable duplet**), it is chemically inert and does not usually participate in chemical bonding. Consequently, its **valency is 0**. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
• Elements in **Group 2** of the modern periodic table, such as **Magnesium (Mg)** and **Calcium (Ca)**, share the same **+2 valency** as Beryllium because they all possess **two valence electrons**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Valency Definition:**

 
 
• **Valency** is defined as the **combining capacity** of an atom of an element. It is determined by the number of **valence electrons** present in the outermost shell of the atom.
 
• For metals in **Groups 1, 2, and 13**, the valency is equal to the number of valence electrons. For non-metals, it is often calculated as **8 minus the number of valence electrons**.
 
 
 
• **Beryllium Characteristics:**
 
 
• **Location:** It is located in **Group 2** and **Period 2** of the **Modern Periodic Table**.
 
• **Features:** It is a **steel-gray**, strong, lightweight, and brittle **alkaline earth metal**. It has a relatively **high melting point** of **1287°C**.
 
• **Uses:** Beryllium is used as an alloying agent in **beryllium copper**, in the construction of **aerospace components**, and as a **neutron moderator** in nuclear reactors.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Table Trends:**
 
 
• Moving **down a group**, the valency remains the **same** because the number of valence electrons is constant.
 
• Moving **across a period** from left to right, the valency first **increases** (from 1 to 4) and then **decreases** (down to 0 for noble gases).
 
 
 
• **Noble Gases:**
 
 
• Elements like **Neon (Ne)**, **Argon (Ar)**, and **Krypton (Kr)** belong to **Group 18**. They have a **completely filled valence shell** (octet), making them stable with a **valency of zero**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Octet Rule:** Atoms tend to gain, lose, or share electrons to achieve a stable configuration of **eight electrons** (or two for the first shell) in their valence shell, known as the **Octet Rule**.
 
• **Electropositive Nature:** Since **Beryllium** loses electrons to form cations (**Be²⁺**), it is considered an **electropositive element**.
 
• **Atomic Radius:** **Beryllium** has a smaller atomic radius compared to other elements in its group (like Magnesium), which results in a higher **ionization energy** within **Group 2**.

questions.question: What happens to a light ray when it passes through the optical centre of a lens?

options.text: It will emerge without any deviation
It passes through the principal focus on the other side of the lens
It bends toward the principal axis
It will emerge parallel to the principal axis

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It will emerge without any deviation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **optical centre** is a point on the **principal axis** of a lens such that any ray of light passing through it does not undergo any **deviation** or **refraction**.
 
• For a **thin lens**, when a light ray passes through the **optical centre**, the incident ray and the emergent ray are **collinear**. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• If a light ray passes through the **principal focus** of a **convex lens**, it will emerge **parallel** to the **principal axis** on the other side. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
• A light ray that is **parallel to the principal axis** will pass through the **principal focus** on the other side after **refraction** in a **convex lens**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The property of no deviation at the **optical centre** applies to both **convex (converging)** and **concave (diverging)** lenses.
 
• In ray diagrams, the **optical centre** is usually represented by the letter **O** or **C**, and it serves as the reference point for measuring all distances like **object distance (u)** and **image distance (v)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Convex Lens**:

 
 
• A **convex lens** is thicker at the **centre** than at the **edges**. It is known as a **converging lens** because it converges parallel rays of light at a single point called the **focus**.
 
• The **focal length** of a convex lens is considered **positive** according to the **Cartesian sign convention**.
 
• It is used in **magnifying glasses**, **cameras**, and to correct **Hypermetropia (long-sightedness)**.
 
 
 
• **Concave Lens**:
 
 
• A **concave lens** is thinner at the **centre** than at the **edges**. It is known as a **diverging lens** because it diverges parallel rays of light.
 
• The **focal length** of a concave lens is always **negative**.
 
• It is commonly used in **flashlights**, **peepholes** in doors, and to correct **Myopia (short-sightedness)**.
 
 
 
• **Refraction**:
 
 
• **Refraction** is the bending of light as it passes from one **transparent medium** to another of different **optical density**.
 
• The **refractive index** of a material determines how much the light will bend. When light enters a **denser medium**, it bends **towards the normal**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lens Formula**: The relationship between the **object distance (u)**, **image distance (v)**, and **focal length (f)** of a lens is given by **1/v - 1/u = 1/f**.
 
• **Power of a Lens**: The **power (P)** of a lens is the **reciprocal** of its **focal length (f)** in **meters**. The **SI unit** of power is **Dioptre (D)**.
 
• **Lateral Displacement**: While a ray through the **optical centre** of a **thin lens** has zero deviation, in a **thick lens**, there might be a very slight **lateral displacement**, although the emergent ray remains parallel to the incident ray.
 
• **Sign Convention**: According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the **optical centre** is the **origin**, and the **direction of incident light** is taken as **positive**.

questions.question: Which of the following bond is made up of a large number of organic compounds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Covalent bond**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Covalent bond** is a chemical bond that involves the **sharing of electron pairs** between atoms. These electron pairs are known as shared pairs or bonding pairs.
 
• Organic compounds are primarily defined by the presence of **Carbon** atoms. Carbon has **four valence electrons**, which allows it to form **four covalent bonds** with other atoms, a property known as **tetravalency**.
 
• The vast majority of **organic molecules**, including **hydrocarbons**, **proteins**, **lipids**, and **carbohydrates**, are held together by covalent bonds because carbon-carbon and carbon-hydrogen bonds are highly **stable** and strong. ***Hence, the covalent bond is the fundamental bond type in organic chemistry.***
 
• Carbon also possesses the unique ability of **catenation**, which is the linkage of atoms of the same element into **long chains** or **rings**. This leads to the formation of millions of different **organic compounds**.
 
• Covalent bonds usually occur between **non-metals**. Since organic chemistry focuses on carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen (all non-metals), covalent bonding is the dominant force. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ionic Bond:**

 
 
• This bond is formed by the **complete transfer of electrons** from one atom to another, typically between a **metal** and a **non-metal**.
 
• It results in the formation of **cations** (positive) and **anions** (negative) that are held together by **electrostatic forces**.
 
• Examples include **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)** and **Magnesium Oxide (MgO)**. These are **inorganic** in nature and typically form **crystalline solids** with high melting points.
 
 
 
• **Metallic Bond:**
 
 
• This bond occurs between atoms of **metallic elements** like **Copper (Cu)**, **Iron (Fe)**, or **Gold (Au)**.
 
• It is characterized by a "**sea of delocalized electrons**" that move freely around a lattice of positive metal ions.
 
• This structure provides metals with their characteristic **conductivity**, **malleability**, and **ductility**.
 
 
 
• **Dipolar Bond (Dipole-Dipole Interaction):**
 
 
• This is a type of **intermolecular force** rather than a primary chemical bond within a molecule.
 
• It occurs between **polar molecules** that have permanent **dipole moments**, where the positive end of one molecule is attracted to the negative end of another.
 
• **Hydrogen bonding** is a specific, strong type of dipolar interaction often found in **water (H2O)** and **DNA** structures.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Bond Strength:**
 
 
• Generally, **Covalent** and **Ionic bonds** are considered primary (strong) bonds, with bond energies typically ranging from **100 to 1000 kJ/mol**.
 
• **Dipolar interactions** are much weaker secondary forces, usually around **5 to 25 kJ/mol**, but they are crucial for determining the **boiling points** and solubility of organic compounds.

• While most organic compounds are covalent, some organic molecules can have **ionic characters**, such as **Soap (Sodium Stearate)**, which contains a long **covalent hydrocarbon chain** and an **ionic head**.

questions.question: When a gun is fired, why does the gun experience a recoil even though the bullet moves forward?

options.text: Because the bullet’s acceleration is less than the gun’s
Because the bullet exerts an equal and opposite force on the gun
Because the gun’s mass is smaller than the bullet’s
Because the gun pushes the bullet forward with less force

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Because the bullet exerts an equal and opposite force on the gun**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phenomenon of a gun moving backward when a bullet is fired is known as **recoil**. This is a direct application of **Newton’s Third Law of Motion**, which states that for every **action**, there is an **equal and opposite reaction**.
 
• When the **gunpowder** in a cartridge explodes, it creates **expanding gases** that exert a huge **force** on the **bullet**, pushing it forward through the barrel. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Simultaneously, according to the **law of action and reaction**, the **bullet** exerts an exactly **equal amount of force** back onto the **gun** in the **opposite direction**.
 
• The **forward motion** of the bullet is the **action**, and the **backward motion** of the gun is the **reaction**.
 
• While the **forces** acting on the gun and the bullet are **equal in magnitude**, their resulting **accelerations** differ significantly because of the vast difference in their **masses**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Law of Conservation of Momentum:**

 
 
• The **recoil of a gun** can also be explained using the **Law of Conservation of Momentum**. This law states that the **total momentum** of an isolated system remains **constant** if no external force acts on it.
 
• Before firing, the **initial momentum** of both the **gun** and the **bullet** is **zero** because they are at **rest**.
 
• After firing, the **final momentum** must also be **zero**. Therefore, the **positive momentum** of the bullet (moving forward) must be balanced by the **negative momentum** of the gun (moving backward).
 
• Mathematically: **m × v + M × V = 0**, where **m** and **v** are the mass and velocity of the bullet, and **M** and **V** are the mass and velocity of the gun.
 
 
 
• **Recoil Velocity:**
 
 
• The **recoil velocity (V)** of the gun is given by **V = -(m × v) / M**.
 
• Because the **mass of the gun (M)** is much **larger** than the **mass of the bullet (m)**, the **recoil velocity** is much **smaller** than the **bullet's velocity**.
 
• This explains why the gun moves back with a **jerk** rather than flying back at the same speed as the bullet.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Second Law in Context:**
 
 
• According to **Newton's Second Law (F = ma)**, for a **constant force**, **acceleration** is **inversely proportional** to **mass**.
 
• The **bullet**, having a **very small mass**, experiences a **tremendous acceleration**. The **gun**, having a **large mass**, experiences a **small acceleration**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Analysis of Incorrect Options:**

 
 
• **Option 1:** The bullet's **acceleration** is actually much **greater** than the gun’s, not less, due to its **smaller mass**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Option 3:** In reality, a **gun's mass** is always **larger** than the **bullet's mass** to minimize the **recoil velocity** and ensure the safety of the user. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Option 4:** According to **Newton’s Third Law**, the **force** pushed by the gun on the bullet and the force pushed by the bullet on the gun are **exactly equal** in magnitude. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• Soldiers are trained to hold a gun **tightly against their shoulder**. This effectively **increases the mass (M)** by adding the **shooter's body mass** to the gun's mass, thereby **reducing the recoil velocity** and preventing injury.
 
• **Muzzle brakes** or **recoil pads** are often used in modern firearms to **absorb** or **redirect** some of the **kinetic energy** generated during the **recoil**.

questions.question: When you sit on a chair, the chair exerts an upward force on you. The reaction force in this case is:

options.text: Friction between your clothes and the chair
Force of air on the chair
Your weight acting downward on the chair

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Your weight acting downward on the chair**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This phenomenon is a direct application of **Newton's Third Law of Motion**, which states that for every **action**, there is always an **equal and opposite reaction**.
 
• When you sit on a chair, your body exerts a **downward force** on the chair. This force is primarily due to your **weight**, which is the **gravitational pull** of the **Earth** acting on your **mass**.
 
• The chair, in turn, exerts an **upward force** on you to support your weight. This upward force is known as the **Normal Force**.
 
• In the context of **action-reaction pairs**, the two forces must act on **different objects**. Here, the **action** is your body pushing down on the chair, and the **reaction** is the chair pushing up on your body. *Hence, the reaction to the chair's upward force is your weight acting downward on it.*
 
• Both forces are **equal in magnitude** but **opposite in direction**. If the chair could not exert an equal upward force, it would break or you would accelerate downwards. *Hence, the statement regarding weight as the reaction force is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's First Law (Inertia):**

 
 
• It states that an object will remain at **rest** or move at a **constant velocity** unless acted upon by an **external unbalanced force**. When sitting still on a chair, the **net force** on you is **zero** because the forces are **balanced**.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Second Law (F=ma):**
 
 
• This law defines **force** as the product of **mass** and **acceleration**. Since you are not moving (acceleration is **0**) while sitting, the sum of the **upward normal force** and **downward gravitational force** equals zero.
 
 
 
• **Contact Forces:**
 
 
• The interaction between your clothes and the chair involves **friction**, but this is a **lateral (horizontal) force** that prevents sliding and is not the reaction to the **vertical upward force**.
 
• The force of **air** on the chair (atmospheric pressure) exists but is **negligible** in this specific mechanical interaction between the person and the furniture.
 
 
 
• **Gravity vs. Weight:**
 
 
• The **gravitational pull of the Earth** is a **non-contact force** acting on your body. Its reaction force is actually the **gravitational pull** your body exerts back on the **Earth**, not the force between you and the chair.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Action-Reaction Pair Characteristics:**

 
 
• They always occur in **pairs** and act **simultaneously**.
 
• They never act on the **same object**; one force acts on **Object A** (the chair) and the other acts on **Object B** (the person).
 
• The **magnitude** of the **Normal Force** is exactly equal to the **Weight** (**mg**) of the person only when the surface is **horizontal** and there are no other vertical forces acting.
 
• In physics, **Weight** is measured in **Newtons (N)**, just like any other **force**, whereas **Mass** is measured in **Kilograms (kg)**.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the universal gravitational constant G?

options.text: It is equal to the acceleration due to gravity.
It is a universal constant, same everywhere.
It varies from place to place on Earth.
It depends on the medium between two masses.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is a universal constant, same everywhere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Universal Gravitational Constant**, denoted by the symbol **G**, is a fundamental physical constant that appears in **Sir Isaac Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation**. It defines the strength of the gravitational attraction between two objects.
 
• **Statement 1**: It is equal to the acceleration due to gravity. This is not true because **G** is a constant of proportionality, whereas **g** (acceleration due to gravity) is the acceleration an object undergoes due to the gravitational pull of a massive body like **Earth**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 2**: It is a universal constant, same everywhere. This is true because the value of **G** does not change regardless of the **location** in the universe, the **time** of measurement, or the **nature** of the bodies involved. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 3**: It varies from place to place on Earth. While the value of **g** (approximately **9.8 m/s²**) varies based on **latitude**, **altitude**, and **depth**, the value of **G** remains absolutely constant at every point on **Earth** and in space. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 4**: It depends on the medium between two masses. Gravitational force is unique compared to electromagnetic forces because it is **independent of the intervening medium**. Whether two masses are in a **vacuum**, **water**, or **solid rock**, the constant **G** and the resulting force remain the same. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is It is a universal constant, same everywhere.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation:**

 
 
• The law states that every point mass attracts every other point mass by a force acting along the line intersecting both points.
 
• The **mathematical formula** is **F = G(m1m2 / r²)**, where **F** is the force, **m1** and **m2** are the masses, and **r** is the distance between their centers.
 
 
 
• **Numerical Value and Units:**
 
 
• The accepted value of **G** is approximately **6.674 x 10^-11 N m² kg&sup-2**.
 
• The **SI units** for **G** are **Newton meter squared per kilogram squared**.
 
• In **base SI units**, it is expressed as **m³ kg&sup-1 s&sup-2**.
 
 
 
• **Dimensions of G:**
 
 
• The **dimensional formula** for the universal gravitational constant is **[M^-1 L³ T^-2]**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Although **Newton** formulated the law in **1687**, the first accurate measurement of **G** was performed by **Henry Cavendish** in **1798** using a **torsion balance** experiment.
 
• This experiment was famously known as "**weighing the Earth**" because knowing **G** allowed for the calculation of the **Earth's mass**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Difference between G and g:**

 
 
• **G** is a **scalar quantity**, whereas **g** is a **vector quantity** (it has a direction toward the center of the mass).
 
• **G** is **Universal**, while **g** is **local** (it is different on the **Moon**, **Mars**, or at the **Equator** vs. the **Poles**).
 
• The value of **g** is derived using **G** through the formula: **g = GM / R²**, where **M** is the mass of the planet and **R** is its radius.
 
 
 
• **Weakest Force:**
 
 
• Gravity is the **weakest** of the **four fundamental forces** of nature (the others being **Electromagnetism**, **Strong Nuclear**, and **Weak Nuclear** forces).
 
• Because **G** is so small (**10^-11**), gravitational attraction is only significant when at least one of the objects has a **massive scale**, such as a **planet** or **star**.

__
 
• **Yeast** is a **unicellular organism** belonging to the **Kingdom Fungi** that reproduces asexually through a process known as **budding**.
 
• In this process, a **small bulb-like projection** or outgrowth appears on the parent cell body, which is scientifically termed a **bud**. ***Hence, statement A is correct.***
 
• As the process progresses, the **nucleus** of the parent yeast cell divides, and one of the daughter nuclei migrates into the developing **bud**.

• Eventually, these **buds** detach from the parent cell and mature into new, independent **yeast cells**, allowing for rapid population growth in a short **time**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Binary Fission:** Observed in organisms like **Amoeba**, where a single cell divides into two equal **daughter cells**.
 
• **Fragmentation:** Seen in **Spirogyra** (an **alga**), where the body breaks into smaller pieces, and each piece grows into a new individual.
 
• **Spore Formation:** Common in **fungi** like **Rhizopus** (bread mould), where **spores** are released into the **air** and germinate under favorable conditions of **moisture** and **temperature**.

• This is a form of **asexual reproduction** in **plants** where new plants are produced from **roots**, **stems**, **leaves**, and **buds** (e.g., **Potato tubers**, **Bryophyllum** leaves).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **budding** process in **Yeast** is distinct because the division of **cytoplasm** is unequal, resulting in a smaller **bud** and a larger **parent cell**, unlike **binary fission** where the division is roughly **equal**.
 
• The formation of a **chain of buds** is a characteristic **feature** of **yeast** when nutrients are abundant, specifically **glucose**.
 
• In **2024**, **yeast** remains a primary **model organism** in **biological research** for studying **cell cycle** and **genetics** due to its simple **unicellular** structure and eukaryotic nature.

questions.question: Which of the following explains a precipitation reaction?

options.text: A reaction involving a color change only
A reaction in which a gas is formed
A reaction where heat is released
A reaction where an insoluble solid is formed

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A reaction where an insoluble solid is formed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **precipitation reaction** is a chemical reaction that occurs in an **aqueous solution** when two **ionic bonds** combine, resulting in the formation of an **insoluble salt**.
 
• The **insoluble solid** that emerges from the liquid solution is called the **precipitate**. This occurs when the **concentration** of dissolved ions exceeds the **solubility product** of the resulting compound. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• These reactions typically involve the exchange of **cations** and **anions** between two **soluble salts** in a liquid environment, often water.
 
• A common **example** is the reaction between **Silver Nitrate (AgNO3)** and **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**. When mixed, they produce a **white precipitate** of **Silver Chloride (AgCl)** and soluble **Sodium Nitrate**.
 
• The general chemical representation for a precipitation reaction is **A(aq) + B(aq) → C(s) + D(aq)**, where **(s)** denotes the **solid state** of the precipitate formed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Color Change Reactions**: A reaction involving a **color change only** (Option 1) is often a characteristic of **Redox reactions** or **Acid-Base reactions** using **indicators**. While a precipitate might have a color, color change alone does not define the formation of a solid. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Gas Evolution**: A reaction in which a **gas is formed** (Option 2) is known as a **gas evolution reaction**. An example is the reaction of **Carbonates with Acids** to release **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)**. This is a distinct category from precipitation. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Exothermic Reactions**: A reaction where **heat is released** (Option 3) is classified as an **exothermic reaction**. While many chemical processes release energy, heat release is not the defining criterion for a precipitation reaction. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Double Displacement**: Most precipitation reactions are **double displacement reactions** (also known as metathesis), where the **reactants** "swap" partners to create a new insoluble product.
 
• **Solubility Rules**: Chemists use **solubility rules** to predict whether a precipitate will form. For instance, salts containing **Alkali Metals** or **Ammonium ions** are generally **soluble**, whereas many **Sulfates** and **Chlorides** of heavy metals are **insoluble**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Industrial Uses**: Precipitation is widely used in **wastewater treatment** to remove **heavy metals** like **Lead** and **Mercury** by turning them into insoluble solids that can be filtered out.
 
• **Analytical Chemistry**: These reactions are essential in **qualitative inorganic analysis** to detect the presence of specific **ions** in a sample based on the color and solubility of the precipitate formed.
 
• **Biological Significance**: In the human body, the formation of **kidney stones** is essentially a precipitation reaction where **Calcium Oxalate** becomes insoluble in the urinary tract.
 
• **Pigment Production**: Many **industrial pigments** used in **paints** and **dyes** are manufactured through controlled precipitation reactions to ensure uniform particle size and **color intensity**.

questions.question: What is the network of tiny tubular structures found in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Endoplasmic reticulum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)** is a complex network of **tiny tubular structures** that are scattered throughout the **cytoplasm** of **eukaryotic cells**.
 
• Electron microscopic studies reveal that the ER divides the **intracellular space** into two distinct compartments: the **luminal** (inside the ER) and the **extra-luminal** (cytoplasm) compartments.
 
• This organelle was first observed by **Keith Porter**, **Albert Claude**, and **Ernest Fullam** in the year **1945**.
 
• The ER is often continuous with the **outer membrane** of the **nucleus** and extends throughout the cell, providing a large **surface area** for various chemical reactions.
 
• It plays a vital role as a **cytoskeletal framework** and acts as a channel for the **transport of materials** between different parts of the cytoplasm or between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Golgi apparatus**:

 
 
• First described by **Camillo Golgi** in **1898**, it consists of flat, disc-shaped sacs called **cisternae** of **0.5μm to 1.0μm** diameter.
 
• Its primary function is the **packaging** and **processing** of proteins and lipids, especially for **secretion**.
 
• It is the site for the formation of **glycoproteins** and **glycolipids**.
 
 
 
• **Lysosome**:
 
 
• These are membrane-bound **vesicular structures** formed by the process of packaging in the Golgi apparatus.
 
• They are rich in almost all types of **hydrolytic enzymes** (hydrolases – lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) which are active at an **acidic pH**.
 
• They are often called **suicidal bags** because they can digest the entire cell if it becomes damaged or dead.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria**:
 
 
• Known as the **powerhouse of the cell**, these double-membrane-bound organelles are responsible for **aerobic respiration**.
 
• They produce cellular energy in the form of **ATP** (Adenosine Triphosphate).
 
• Mitochondria possess their own **DNA** and **70S ribosomes**, making them semi-autonomous organelles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Types of Endoplasmic Reticulum**:

 
 
• **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)**: It bears **ribosomes** on its surface. It is actively involved in **protein synthesis** and secretion. It is extensive and continuous with the outer membrane of the nucleus.
 
• **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)**: It lacks **ribosomes**. It is the major site for the synthesis of **lipids** and **steroid hormones**. In animal cells, lipid-like steroid hormones are synthesized in SER.
 
 
 
• **Detoxification**: In the **liver cells** of vertebrates, the SER plays a crucial role in **detoxifying** many poisons and drugs.
 
• **Sarcoplasmic Reticulum**: A specialized type of smooth ER found in **muscle cells** that regulates **calcium ion** concentration, which is essential for muscle contraction.

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics of connective tissue is INCORRECT?

• ***Hence, the incorrect statement (and correct answer) is that cells are tightly arranged.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Connective Tissue:**

 
 
• **Loose Connective Tissue:** Cells and fibers are loosely arranged in a semi-fluid ground substance. Examples include **Areolar tissue** (found beneath the skin) and **Adipose tissue** (specialized for fat storage).
 
• **Dense Connective Tissue:** Fibers and fibroblasts are compactly packed. This includes **Dense Regular** (like **tendons** and **ligaments**) and **Dense Irregular** tissues.
 
• **Specialized Connective Tissue:** This category includes **Cartilage**, **Bones**, and **Blood**.
 
 
 
• **Functions and Features:**
 
 
• **Bone:** Has a hard and non-pliable ground substance rich in **calcium salts** and **collagen fibers** which give bone its strength. It provides the structural frame for the body.
 
• **Cartilage:** The intercellular material is solid and pliable and resists compression. It is found in the **tip of the nose**, **outer ear joints**, and between adjacent bones of the vertebral column.
 
• **Adipose Tissue:** Located mainly beneath the skin, the cells of this tissue are specialized to **store fats**. The excess of nutrients which are not utilized immediately are converted into fats and stored here.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Fibroblasts:** These are the most common cells in connective tissue proper that produce and secrete the **extracellular matrix** and **fibers** like **collagen**.
 
• **Tendons and Ligaments:** **Tendons** are dense regular connective tissues that attach **skeletal muscles to bones**, while **ligaments** attach **one bone to another**.
 
• **Cellularity vs. Matrix:** One of the easiest ways to distinguish between tissue types is the ratio of cells to matrix. **Epithelial tissues** have high cellularity and minimal matrix, whereas **Connective tissues** have low cellularity and an extensive matrix.
 
• **Vascularity:** Most connective tissues are highly **vascular** (rich blood supply), with the notable exception of **cartilage**, which is **avascular** and heals slowly.

questions.question: A concave mirror can form a real and inverted image when the object is placed:
questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**Beyond the centre of curvature**__.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave mirror** is a spherical mirror with an inwardly curved reflecting surface. It is also known as a **converging mirror** because it converges light rays that strike its surface.
 
• When an object is placed **Beyond the centre of curvature (C)**, the light rays from the object converge after reflection to form an image between the **focus (F)** and the **centre of curvature (C)**. The nature of this image is **real**, **inverted**, and **diminished**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• When the object is placed **Between the focus (F) and the pole (P)**, the reflected rays diverge and appear to meet behind the mirror. This results in a **virtual**, **erect**, and **magnified** image. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• If an object is placed **At the focus (F)**, the reflected rays become parallel to each other. Theoretically, the image is formed at **infinity**, and it is **real**, **inverted**, and **highly magnified**. ***Hence, while it is real/inverted, it is a specific case of infinity.***
 
• Placing an object **Very close to the mirror** (between the pole and the focus) is the only position where a **concave mirror** produces a **virtual and erect** image rather than a **real and inverted** one. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Image Formation Table for Concave Mirror:**

 
 
• **At infinity**: Image is formed **at the focus (F)**, is **real**, **inverted**, and **point-sized**.
 
• **At the centre of curvature (C)**: Image is formed **at C**, is **real**, **inverted**, and **the same size** as the object.
 
• **Between C and F**: Image is formed **beyond C**, is **real**, **inverted**, and **magnified**.
 
 
 
• **Sign Convention and Formulae:**
 
 
• The **Mirror Formula** is given by **1/v + 1/u = 1/f**, where **v** is the image distance, **u** is the object distance, and **f** is the **focal length**.
 
• **Magnification (m)** is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object, expressed as **m = -v/u**. A **negative magnification** indicates a **real and inverted** image.
 
• For a **concave mirror**, the **focal length (f)** and **radius of curvature (R)** are always taken as **negative** according to the **Cartesian sign convention**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Concave Mirrors:**
 
 
• Used as **shaving mirrors** or **makeup mirrors** to see an enlarged image of the face.
 
• Used by **dentists** to see large images of the teeth of patients.
 
• Used in **solar furnaces** to concentrate sunlight to produce high heat.
 
• Used in **headlights** of vehicles and **searchlights** to get powerful parallel beams of light.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Radius of Curvature:** The distance between the **pole (P)** and the **centre of curvature (C)** is called the **radius of curvature (R)**. The relationship between **f** and **R** is **R = 2f**.
 
• **Real vs. Virtual Image:** A **real image** is formed when light rays actually meet at a point after reflection and can be obtained on a **screen**. A **virtual image** is formed when light rays appear to diverge from a point and **cannot** be obtained on a screen.
 
• **Principal Axis:** The imaginary line passing through the **pole** and the **centre of curvature** of a spherical mirror is called the **principal axis**.
 
• **Aperture:** The diameter of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror is called its **aperture**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a property of suspension?

options.text: Particles cannot be seen by naked eyes.
Solute particles cannot be separated by the process of filtration

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Suspension is a heterogeneous mixture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **suspension** is defined as a **heterogeneous mixture** where the **solute particles** do not dissolve in the **solvent** but instead remain suspended throughout the bulk of the medium. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The particles of a **suspension** are quite large, typically with a **diameter greater than 1000 nm** (or 10⁻⁶ meters), which makes them easily **visible to the naked eye**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Suspensions are inherently **unstable**. If a suspension is allowed to stand **undisturbed**, the heavy **solute particles settle down** at the bottom of the container due to the **force of gravity**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Due to the significant size of the particles, they **can be separated** from the liquid or gas medium using simple physical methods like **filtration**. The particles are trapped by the filter paper while the liquid passes through. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• When particles are suspended and have not yet settled, they are capable of **scattering a beam of light** passing through the mixture, making the path of light visible; this phenomenon is known as the **Tyndall effect**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Mixtures based on Particle Size:**

 
 
• **True Solution:** This is a **homogeneous mixture** where the particle size is less than **1 nm**. These particles do not scatter light and cannot be seen even with a microscope. Examples include **salt in water** and **sugar in water**.
 
• **Colloidal Solution:** These appear homogeneous but are actually **heterogeneous**. The particle size ranges between **1 nm and 1000 nm**. They show the **Tyndall effect** and do not settle over time. Examples include **milk**, **fog**, and **blood**.
 
• **Suspension:** As discussed, these are **heterogeneous** with particles larger than **1000 nm**. Common examples include **muddy water**, **chalk powder in water**, and **dust particles in the air**.
 
 
 
• **Filtration Process:**
 
 
• In a suspension, the **solid phase** is dispersed in the **liquid phase**. Because the pores of standard **filter paper** are smaller than the suspended particles, **filtration** is an effective **separation technique**.
 
• Once the particles **settle down**, the suspension effectively ceases to exist as the mixture is no longer uniform, and it loses its ability to scatter light.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Stability:** The **stability** of a mixture is a key identifying feature. **Solutions** and **colloids** are considered **stable** because their particles remain dispersed indefinitely. **Suspensions** are **unstable** because the components eventually separate into distinct layers.
 
• **Optical Properties:** While **suspensions** show the **Tyndall effect** when the particles are floating, once the particles **precipitate** or settle at the bottom, the remaining liquid above typically stops scattering light.
 
• **Naked Eye Visibility:** The threshold for **naked eye visibility** is generally around **0.1 millimeters**. Since suspension particles are often larger than this or clump together, they are easily distinguishable without magnification, unlike the components of **homogeneous mixtures**.

questions.question: A school organises a 'Zero Waste' day. Which of the following practices will best support this initiative?

options.text: Disposing food waste in regular trash bins
Serving food in banana leaves or reusable plates

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Serving food in banana leaves or reusable plates**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **'Zero Waste'** initiative is a philosophy and a design principle for the **21st Century** that includes the "no-waste" approach, aiming to guide people in changing their lifestyles and practices to emulate sustainable natural cycles.
 
• **Serving food in banana leaves or reusable plates** is the most effective practice because it eliminates the generation of trash. **Banana leaves** are completely **biodegradable** and **compostable**, while **reusable plates** (made of **stainless steel**, **ceramic**, or **glass**) can be washed and used thousands of times, preventing material from entering the waste stream. ***Hence, this statement is correct.***
 
• Using **single-use plastic cutlery** involves items like spoons and forks that are discarded after one use. These are typically made from **polystyrene** or **polypropylene**, which take hundreds of years to decompose in **landfills** and often end up polluting **oceans**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Disposing food waste in regular trash bins** prevents organic matter from being composted. When organic waste is sent to **landfills**, it undergoes **anaerobic decomposition** and produces **methane**, a potent greenhouse gas that contributes to **climate change**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Wrapping snacks in plastic foil** or aluminum foil creates immediate waste once the snack is consumed. **Plastic wraps** are difficult to recycle due to their thinness and chemical composition, frequently leading to **microplastic** contamination in the environment. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The 5 R's of Waste Management**: To achieve zero waste, individuals and institutions follow the hierarchy of **Refuse** (saying no to single-use items), **Reduce** (consuming less), **Reuse** (using items repeatedly), **Recycle** (processing materials to make new products), and **Rot** (composting organic matter).
 
• **Single-Use Plastic Ban in India**: The **Government of India** implemented a nationwide ban on identified **Single-Use Plastic (SUP)** items with effect from **July 1, 2022**. This includes items with low utility and high littering potential, such as plastic sticks for balloons, plastic flags, and **thermocol** for decoration.
 
• **Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016**: These rules in **India** emphasize **source segregation** of waste into three streams: **Biodegradable** (wet), **Non-biodegradable** (dry), and **Domestic Hazardous waste**. Schools and bulk generators are mandated to process biodegradable waste through **composting** or **biomethanation** within their premises.
 
• **Circular Economy**: A **Zero Waste** approach is a key component of a **Circular Economy**, which moves away from the traditional **linear economy** (take-make-dispose) model. It focuses on keeping resources in use for as long as possible to extract the maximum value.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Environmental Impact of Plastics**: Plastics are **petroleum-based** synthetic polymers. **Microplastics** (particles less than **5mm**) have been found in **drinking water**, **food chains**, and even **human blood**, posing significant health risks.
 
• **Banana Leaves Benefits**: Beyond being eco-friendly, **banana leaves** contain **polyphenols** (natural antioxidants) like **EGCG**, which can be absorbed by the food served on them. They are widely used in **South India**, **Philippines**, and **Thailand** as a traditional, hygienic, and cost-effective serving medium.
 
• **Waste Audits**: For a school to successfully implement a **'Zero Waste'** day, it often conducts a **Waste Audit**, which is a formal process used to quantify the amount and types of waste being generated, helping to identify areas for waste reduction.

questions.question: Which of the following methods of asexual reproduction allows a new organism to develop from a cut or broken body part?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fragmentation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fragmentation** is a type of **asexual reproduction** in which a multicellular organism breaks into two or more fragments upon maturation.
 
• In this process, each **cut or broken body part** develops into a fully functional, independent **new organism**.
 
• This method is typically seen in organisms with relatively simple body designs, such as **Spirogyra** (a filamentous green algae) and **Planaria** (flatworms). ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• In **Spirogyra**, when the filament reaches a certain length, it simply breaks into smaller pieces, and each piece continues to grow through cell division to form a new individual.
 
• While similar to **regeneration**, fragmentation is considered a deliberate reproductive strategy in these organisms, allowing for rapid population growth in favorable environments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Spore Formation**:

 
 
• This is a method of reproduction used by many **Fungi** (like **Rhizopus** or bread mold), **Ferns**, and **Mosses**.
 
• Organisms produce microscopic, unicellular reproductive bodies called **spores** covered by a hard protective coat to withstand unfavorable conditions. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Budding**:
 
 
• In this process, a small projection or **bud** grows out from the body of the parent organism due to repeated **mitotic cell divisions**.
 
• The bud matures and eventually detaches to live as an independent organism. Common examples include **Yeast** and **Hydra**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Binary Fission**:
 
 
• This is a form of asexual reproduction where a **single-celled organism** divides into two equal halves.
 
• It is commonly seen in **Prokaryotes** (Bacteria) and **Protists** like **Amoeba**, **Paramecium**, and **Leishmania**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Asexual Reproduction**:
 
 
• It involves only a **single parent** and does not require the fusion of **gametes** (sperm and egg).
 
• The resulting offspring are **genetically identical** to the parent and are often referred to as **clones**.
 
• Other types include **Vegetative Propagation**, which is used by plants like **Potato**, **Ginger**, and **Bryophyllum** to grow new plants from vegetative parts like **roots**, **stems**, or **leaves**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Difference between Fragmentation and Regeneration**: While **Fragmentation** is a reproductive method for simple organisms, **Regeneration** is the ability of an organism to regrow lost body parts (like a **Lizard's tail** or **Starfish arms**).
 
• In highly complex multicellular organisms, fragmentation is not possible because cells are organized into **tissues**, which are organized into **organs**, and finally **organ systems**, requiring specialized cells for reproduction.
 
• The process of fragmentation is often triggered by **physical disturbances** or **natural maturation** cycles in aquatic environments.

questions.question: A sound wave has a frequency of 250 Hz. The time taken for one complete vibration is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.004 s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Frequency (f)** is defined as the **number of complete vibrations** or cycles that occur in **one second**. It is measured in **Hertz (Hz)**, where **1 Hz** equals **one vibration per second**.
 
• The **Time Period (T)** is the time required for the wave to complete **one full vibration** or cycle.
 
• There is an inverse relationship between **frequency** and **time period**, which is expressed by the mathematical formula: **T = 1 / f**.
 
• In this specific problem, the **frequency** is given as **250 Hz**. By applying the formula, the calculation becomes **T = 1 / 250**.
 
• Dividing **1** by **250** gives a numerical value of **0.004**. Therefore, the **time taken** for **one complete vibration** is **0.004 s**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the time period being 0.004 s is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sound Waves:**

 
 
• Sound is a **mechanical wave** that requires a **medium** (solid, liquid, or gas) to propagate. It travels as a **longitudinal wave**, where particles of the medium vibrate parallel to the direction of wave travel.
 
• The **speed of sound** depends on the **nature of the medium** and the **temperature**. For example, sound travels at approximately **343 meters per second** in **air** at **20 degrees Celsius**, but much faster in **water** (about **1,480 meters per second**) and **solids** like **steel** (about **5,960 meters per second**).
 
 
 
• **Audible Range:**
 
 
• The **human ear** can typically hear frequencies ranging from **20 Hz** to **20,000 Hz (20 kHz)**.
 
• Frequencies below **20 Hz** are known as **infrasonic** sound, while frequencies above **20,000 Hz** are called **ultrasonic** sound.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Sound:**
 
 
• **Pitch:** This is determined by the **frequency** of the sound wave. A higher frequency results in a **higher pitch**.
 
• **Loudness:** This depends on the **amplitude** of the vibration. It is measured in **decibels (dB)**.
 
• **Quality (Timbre):** This allows the ear to distinguish between sounds of the same **pitch** and **loudness** produced by different sources.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mathematical Relations:** The **velocity (v)** of a sound wave is the product of its **frequency (f)** and its **wavelength (lambda)**. This is written as **v = f × lambda**.
 
• **Hertz:** The unit **Hertz** is named after the **German physicist Heinrich Rudolf Hertz**, who was the first to provide conclusive proof of the existence of electromagnetic waves in the **year 1887**.
 
• **Time Period Conversion:** In physics problems, if the **time period** is given in **milliseconds (ms)**, it must be converted to **seconds (s)** by dividing by **1,000** to ensure consistency with **SI units**. For instance, **4 ms** is equal to **0.004 s**.
 
• **Oscillation:** A complete back-and-forth motion is called an **oscillation**. The **time period** is effectively the duration of **one oscillation**.

questions.question: The average age of 38 students of a class is 21 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 22 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Age of new person = New Average + (Previous members × Increase in average)

Age of Teacher = 22 + (38 × (22 − 21))

Age of Teacher = 22 + (38 × 1)

Age of Teacher = 22 + 38 = 60 years

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial students = 38, Initial Average = 21 years

New Average (including teacher) = 22 years

**Formula Used:**

Average = Total Sum of values ÷ Number of values

Total Sum = Average × Number of values

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c416d1357bafc2212bc1c950c2b9a878799b46c00703167a5afa706de24ea911.png] 

⇒ Total age of 38 students = 38 × 21 = 798 years

⇒ Total number of people including teacher = 38 + 1 = 39

⇒ Total age of 39 people = 39 × 22 = 858 years

⇒ Age of the teacher = (Total age of 39 people) − (Total age of 38 students)

⇒ Age of the teacher = 858 − 798 = 60 years

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When two groups are combined, the combined average is (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Net Deviation

The sum of deviations of all observations from the average is always zero.

Average Inclusion Rule

If the new value is greater than the original average, the overall average increases; if smaller, it decreases.

questions.question: During a New-Year sale, a company gives a ‘Buy 9 Sweaters and Get 1 Free’ offer to customers. The percentage discount involved in this deal is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In 'Buy X Get Y Free' offers, the discount is calculated on the total number of items.

Total Items = Paid Items + Free Items = 9 + 1 = 10

Discount % = (Free Items ÷ Total Items) × 100

Discount % = (1 ÷ 10) × 100 = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Buy = 9 sweaters, Free = 1 sweater.

Formula: Discount % = [Free Items ÷ (Buy Items + Free Items)] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b62d4a16409d2d9cfbdfb6c628c11b58ac9bea12370ff2ba692bfd6343ce7c28.png] 

Let the Marked Price (MP) of each sweater be ₹1.

⇒ Total MP for 10 sweaters = 10 × 1 = ₹10

⇒ Customer pays for only 9 sweaters.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) for 10 sweaters = 9 × 1 = ₹9

⇒ Discount Amount = MP − SP = 10 − 9 = ₹1

⇒ Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (1 ÷ 10) × 100 = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

Successive Discounts

When two discounts d₁ and d₂ are applied, effective discount = d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 100.

Markup Percentage

Markup % is the percentage by which MP is higher than CP: [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Profit and Discount Relationship

The ratio of MP to CP is given by: MP/CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

questions.question: If 9 is subtracted from the numerator of a fraction, it becomes (2)/(9) , and if 12 is added to the denominator of the fraction, it becomes (1)/(3) . What is the sum of the numerator and the denominator of the original fraction?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the original fraction be x/y.

According to the conditions: 9(x − 9) = 2y and 3x = y + 12.

From the second eq, y = 3x − 12. Substitute this in the first eq.

9x − 81 = 2(3x − 12) ⇒ 9x − 81 = 6x − 24 ⇒ 3x = 57 ⇒ x = 19.

Then, y = 3(19) − 12 = 45. Sum = 19 + 45 = 64.

**∴ The correct answer is 64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Let the fraction be x/y.

Condition 1: (x − 9)/y = 2/9

Condition 2: x/(y + 12) = 1/3

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4c8aa37d2284f817e6b376ea8b9185231aa1bab1a30b1369c602a3c1145dffd7.png] 

From Condition 1:

⇒ 9(x − 9) = 2y

⇒ 9x − 81 = 2y → (Eq. 1)

From Condition 2:

⇒ 3x = y + 12

⇒ y = 3x − 12 → (Eq. 2)

Substitute y from (Eq. 2) into (Eq. 1):

⇒ 9x − 81 = 2(3x − 12)

⇒ 9x − 81 = 6x − 24

⇒ 3x = 57

⇒ x = 19

Substitute x = 19 in (Eq. 2):

⇒ y = 3(19) − 12 = 45

Sum of numerator and denominator:

⇒ x + y = 19 + 45 = 64

**∴ The correct answer is 64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

A proper fraction has a numerator less than the denominator (e.g., 2/9), while an improper fraction has a numerator greater than or equal to the denominator.

Fractions that represent the same value even though they look different, obtained by multiplying or dividing both N and D by the same non-zero number.
